intent: Looped in-place standing idle with a slumped/downward upper-body posture, broad whole-body turn and lateral sway, asymmetric arm follow-through, and a clear kick-like right-leg gesture: lift/flex, rapid reposition, outward swing/extension, then recovery. The leg gesture is not treated as an attack because impact/contact is not evidenced.

phases.name: build-turn-and-sway
phases.description: Turn/sway builds to the canonical body-yaw extreme.

phases.name: right-leg-lift-and-pelvis-plus-x-excursion
phases.description: The pelvis continues toward canonical +X while the right leg lifts/flexes strongly; RightLowerLeg, RightFoot and RightToe reach their pose extremes at f30, then the distal leg reverses fastest around f37-f38. The phase ends at the pelvis +X maximum at f38.

phases.name: right-leg-outward-swing-and-pelvis-rebound
phases.description: The pelvis reverses lateral travel and rises while the right leg continues its outward swing/extension; RightUpperLeg reaches its global pose extreme at f50, followed by the pelvis high rebound at f56.

phases.name: right-leg-recovery-and-secondary-settle
phases.description: The right leg recovers toward stance while the body enters a secondary downward settle, reaching the late pelvis low at f68.

phases.name: loop-return
phases.description: The body returns toward the loop-start state.

keyPoses.description: Reference pose at the start of the loop.
The body reaches its canonical yaw extreme.
The right leg is most strongly raised/flexed in the distal tracks; RightLowerLeg is about 70.29 degrees, RightFoot about 96.05 degrees and RightToe about 96.36 degrees from f0.

keyPoses.role: pelvis +X apex and rapid right-leg reversal
keyPoses.description: The pelvis reaches its maximum canonical +X excursion while RightLowerLeg and RightFoot are in the fastest-reversal region of the right-leg gesture.
RightUpperLeg reaches its global pose extreme at about 17.27 degrees from f0; visually, the right leg has swung/extended outward.
The pelvis reaches its highest position after the lateral apex; the Neck also reaches its rotational peak.

keyPoses.role: late secondary pelvis low / leg recovery
keyPoses.description: The pelvis reaches the later secondary low while the right-leg gesture has recovered close to stance.
Loop endpoint; Root and Hips tracks match f0.

weightTransfer.description: The pelvis shifts clearly toward canonical +X while body yaw reaches its extreme earlier at f16. During this shift, the right leg lifts and changes pose strongly; the pelvis then reaches its lateral apex at f38, rises to f56, drops to the later low at f68, and returns toward the loop endpoint. This supports a slow body-sway / weight-shift description combined with a kick-like right-leg gesture.
weightTransfer.contactCaveat: The exact support/load-bearing foot is not established because animation.json provides no dedicated contact or load-force channel.

bodyMechanics.description: Whole-body coordination is staggered and asymmetric, and the right-leg gesture is a major event rather than minor secondary motion. LeftUpperArm peaks at f22 (about 17.2 degrees) while the right-leg gesture is building; RightLowerLeg, RightFoot and RightToe reach pose extremes together at f30 (about 70.29 / 96.05 / 96.36 degrees); Head peaks at f36 (about 22.36 degrees) while the right leg starts reversing; RightToe changes fastest at f37, RightLowerLeg and RightFoot at f38; Chest peaks at f49 (about 16.66 degrees); RightUpperLeg reaches its global pose peak at f50 (about 17.27 degrees) with Hips rotational departure of about 10.89 degrees; Neck peaks at f56 (about 16.43 degrees) with the pelvis high rebound. This supports the observed sequence right-leg lift/flex -> rapid lower-leg/foot reposition -> outward swing/extension -> recovery, coordinated out of phase with pelvis, torso, head and arms. It is not treated as a proven causal power chain and does not assert impact.

recommended: in-place standing idle with a slumped/downward upper-body posture
broad in-place whole-body turn and lateral sway
kick-like right-leg idle gesture: lift/flex -> rapid reposition -> outward swing/extension -> recovery
pelvis reversal, rebound and loop-return timing coordinated with the right-leg gesture
notRecommended: a combat kick with established contact or impact
